title: 全球氣溫首度連續六天比工業化前高出 2 度
paras: For the first time on record, the average temperature of the planet stayed more than 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels for six days in a row. Pre-industrial means the years from 1850 to 1900, before heavy use of coal and oil. The data came from Copernicus, the climate service of the EU. The highest daily value, 2.24 degrees, was reached on November 23.

Scientists say a strong El Nino is adding heat. El Nino is a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean that happens every few years. They also explain that the Paris Agreement limits are measured over many years, so a few hot days do not mean the limits are broken yet. Still, it is a clear warning.

questions.q: What happened for the first time on record?
options: The ocean froze for six days
Global heat stayed above 2 degrees for six days
Coal use stopped for a week
questions.why: 第一段：全球平均氣溫首度連續六天比工業化前高出 2 度以上。

questions.q: According to scientists, what is El Nino?
options: A satellite of the European Union
A type of coal power plant
A natural warming of the Pacific Ocean
questions.why: 第二段：聖嬰現象（El Nino）是太平洋每隔幾年自然發生的變暖。

questions.q: Why are the Paris Agreement limits not broken yet?
options: They are measured over many years
questions.why: 第二段：巴黎協定的上限是看很多年的平均，幾天很熱不代表已經超過。
